concept.title: Who Counts As Medically Frail
concept.shortdesc: Federal law treats five groups of people as medically frail, and each state turns those groups into its own list of qualifying conditions.

dlentry.dd: As defined in section 1614 of the Social Security Act.
Unless the person has been in stable recovery for five years or more.
A mental health condition that is disabling.
One that significantly limits at least one activity of daily living.
One that is life-threatening, seriously disabling, causes significant pain or needs frequent monitoring, among other descriptors in the rule.

section.title: Your State's Condition List
section.p: Every state must keep a written list of the diseases, diagnoses and conditions that qualify. CMS requires the list to be auditable and justifiable, and states must revise it regularly to add or remove conditions.

section.title: Conditions Not On The List
section.p: Members whose condition isn't listed must have a reasonable way to request that the state consider it.
